title: Perioperative medicine: which drugs to hold, and who needs testing

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the ACC/AHA perioperative cardiovascular evaluation guideline and standard perioperative medicine practice. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: A patient on long-term metoprolol is having elective surgery. What happens to the beta blocker?
questions.a: Continue it, including the morning of surgery
d: Double the dose the morning of surgery
Start it only if the heart rate rises
questions.why: Withdrawal raises perioperative cardiac events. Starting a beta blocker fresh on the day of surgery is the thing to avoid, since it increased stroke and death in trials.

questions.q: How many days before elective surgery is warfarin stopped?
questions.why: The INR is checked the day before and vitamin K given if it is still raised. Warfarin restarts 12 to 24 hours after surgery once haemostasis is secure.

questions.q: Which patients on warfarin need bridging with heparin around surgery?
a: Venous thromboembolism within the past 3 months
Atrial fibrillation with a recent stroke
d: Atrial fibrillation with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 2
A bileaflet aortic valve with no other risk factors
questions.why: Routine bridging in ordinary atrial fibrillation doubled bleeding without reducing thromboembolism in the BRIDGE trial. Only high thrombotic risk justifies it.

questions.q: For a procedure with high bleeding risk, how long before surgery is apixaban stopped in a patient with normal kidney function?
questions.why: One day for low bleeding risk. Direct oral anticoagulants are never bridged; their short half-life is the whole point. Dabigatran needs longer when creatinine clearance is under 50.

questions.q: After a drug-eluting coronary stent, how long should elective surgery that requires stopping the P2Y12 inhibitor be delayed?
questions.why: Aspirin continues through surgery whenever possible. Delay can be shortened to 3 months when the risk of postponing surgery outweighs the risk of stent thrombosis.

questions.q: Which drug should be held on the morning of surgery?
questions.why: Statins are continued and even started before vascular surgery. SGLT-2 inhibitors are held for three to four days beforehand because of ketoacidosis risk.

questions.q: Above what daily prednisone dose, taken for more than three weeks, is adrenal suppression assumed and stress-dose steroid considered?
questions.why: For minor procedures the usual morning dose is enough. For major surgery, hydrocortisone is given at induction and tapered over a day or two.

questions.q: Which are components of the Revised Cardiac Risk Index?
questions.why: Prior stroke or TIA is the sixth. Two or more points means elevated risk, and then functional capacity decides whether any testing is needed at all.

questions.q: A patient at elevated cardiac risk can climb two flights of stairs without symptoms. What functional capacity does that represent, and what does it mean for testing?
questions.a: 4 METs or more; proceed to surgery without stress testing
d: 10 METs; an echocardiogram is still needed
It is not relevant to testing
options: 4 METs or more; proceed to surgery without stress testing
10 METs; an echocardiogram is still needed
It is not relevant to testing
questions.why: Testing is reserved for patients with poor or unknown capacity where the result would change management. A stress test that would not alter the plan is not done.

questions.q: Which preoperative tests are routine for a healthy patient having a low-risk operation?
d: A full blood count and electrolytes
questions.why: Tests are ordered for a reason found in the history or examination, or because the surgery itself demands them. Routine panels find incidental results that delay surgery without improving outcomes.

questions.q: Which screening tool identifies patients at risk of obstructive sleep apnoea before surgery?
questions.why: A high score changes anaesthetic planning and postoperative monitoring, particularly with opioids. Formal sleep studies rarely delay surgery.

questions.q: How far before surgery does stopping smoking measurably reduce complications?
questions.why: Even a day helps carbon monoxide levels, but wound and pulmonary complications fall with four or more weeks. Every preoperative visit is a chance to start.
